answers.text: You did not. Our timeline takes place after the Ethernere breach in EQ1/EQ2, but isn't the same timeline as our timeline was made up of the memories of the souls who never were guided due to the Ethernere's disruptuon. Their energy amassed across the extraplanar space, and worlds from the memories of both the lost and those who found their way. If you're familiar with Seeds of Destruction, you may also remember the Void, and this is adjacent to where this other time was created. Much like Zebuxoruk claimed forbidden knowledge, adventurers in our timeline are able to channel the power of the Ethernere to change the reality around them. This is the reason why we are so powerful in Legends; we've got multiple souls of adventurers and legends inside of us. We have the power to shape the world around us. We're given the power of change. Power is a double edged sword, and with it comes benefits and consequences. Some are less apparent than others.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: This is amazing. I played EQ as an 11 year old back in the day, and then again and again i would return and depart from Norrath. I LOVED this lore hit. How can I maximize me exposure to EQ Lore? Both EQL and EQ Live Lore so I can get more into the RP of it all?

answers.author: Secrets
answers.text: For maximum EQ lore nostalgia, I'd recommend the following: * Claim one of the boosts on EQ1 and go through the Planes of Power raid progression with a merc, and the Seeds of Destruction through Call of the Forsaken content on EQ1. It's very lore relevant to understanding how Legends exists and it's a very well-done story, IMO. Oh, and go to the demiplane of blood and beat up Mayong... again... for me while you're there. * The Lore and Legend server on EQ2 (Kael Drakkal) so you can play the content at the intended difficulty by yourself. Great way to experience some of the questlines (eg; the entire Chains of Eternity expansion and the Destiny of Velious line into Skyshrine, which is one of my favorites from a lore perspective) and have a bit of fun. * Get a copy of the White Wolf EQ Pen and Paper RPG Player's Guide and Gamemaster's Guide if you can swing it. It's old, but very lore relevant as it was penned alongside the original development team. There's a ton of that lore in there that isn't canon, but there's equally a lot that is, and since we're dealing with an alternate reality, anything can happen. EQ2 has a lot of historical lore that fills in a lot of EQ1 gaps, surprisingly. It's why I loved the game when I was younger, and it grew a newfound appreciation for the lore as a setting.

answers.author: Gannor
answers.text: Ah, yes, the Channeler. They were incredibly arkward. Effectively a Bow Healer/DPS SuperHybrid, the Pet was supposed to be a "conduit" for channelling spirit power. The concept was actually based around the Ethernere plotline. The Truespirit were trying to help mend the damage from the Ethernere's influence, and Channelers were the Truespirits' Chosen, whos purpose was to find corruption caused by outside influences and knit up the holes in reality. They were really unfairly powerful when released, and were supposed to be held back by a mechanic that built up corruption inside their spirit, but after people realized you could safely ignore the corruption and just burn, they got nerfed a bit. After the Nerf, they were really more like Gimmick Healers. Never really caught on after that.

With the level of complexity that Tinkering has in EQ2, with everyone able to learn the skill freely, why not turn it into a Class all its own? And you can even fit the same mechanical function. answers.author: Gannor
answers.text: Zebuxoruk is something of a mystery, and his status can change depending on who you ask or what you believe. Some accounts say he was the God of Knowledge, when the world was still young, among many unfamiliar Gods that have long since vanished to time. Some say he was a mortal man who somehow became connected to Knowledge that he shouldn't have. Some claim he's an avatar of the collective will of all mortal life forms. Whatever his true origin, he has preternatural knowledge of time and space. He's a being who has been to the end, witnessed it, and returned to the begining, over and over again. He's a being who has wept in despair for all life, while casually manipulating history to try and prevent the end. In the old times, when the world was new, he founded a City of Refuge called "Zebuxor", in his image. People from all over the world came to him to study; Wise hermits, desperate seekers, fallen priests, penetent villains, greedy adventurers... all were welcome. True neutrality and cooperation for the sake of potential... the sake of power. Zebuxoruk had hoped that by empowering the Mortals of Norrath, without regard for alignment, cause or desire, that he could make them all equal to the Gods themselves, and that then he'd have a power capable of averting the end of time. An army that could finally win the battle at the Alabaster Tower. But the Pantheon caught wind of how much power he was offering th Mortals. The idea that Mortals could ever become equal to the Gods was abhorrent... unforgivable... unalowable. Somehow, they lured Zebuxoruk away from the city that worshipped his name, and in a single night of utter blood... wiped it out to the very last soul.

answers.author: Gannor
answers.text: Zebuxoruk, by some tellings of it, became so enraged by the Gods' sabotage that he decided to spite them. If he could not empower champions from all of Norrath, he'd impart his secrets to the worst of Norrath... the greediest, slimiest, most brutally genius and rotten soul Norrath had seen to that date. The Shissar Emperor, Ssraeshza. He handed over the secrets of Undeath and Soul-Manipulation, Planar Portals and Astral Vision. Enough that the Shissar were able to invade, slaughter, and *eat* a Goddess. Zebuxoruk hadn't expected that. He expected them to become powerful, but to destabilize the cosmos, to risk tearing apart reality could cause the very Discord he fought to take root far too early. Zebuxoruk wept, and allowed himself to be taken prisoner by the Pantheon.

answers.author: Gannor
answers.text: He was sentenced by the Tribunal to eternal imprisonment, and stripped of his Godly Sphere of Influence. He became the Ungod... forgotten... lost at the heart of the Plane of Time. And So, it should have remained. And yet, somehow, his power reached beyond the deepest pits of the astral worlds. He was able to sense Mortals who had become strong enough to battle the Gods themselves, thousands of years later. He called to them, put them on the paths of plots the Gods enacted against them. Exposed Rallos Zek and Solusek Ro's intention to scour the world clean and start again.

answers.author: Gannor
answers.text: Don't forget Roley DeFarge, the previous Commander of the Knights of Truth. He was very highly prasied and respected, but became so obsesse with keeping up his prestige that he started abandoning the city to go on heroic 'quests'. Eventually, those quests turned him into lunch for Mayong Mistmoore, and now he lives as a high-rank Second Generation Vampire under Mayong's control. The anxiety and loss of faith Roley caused in the Freeport Citizens is the reason Valeron Dushire needed a grand task like the Crusade of Tears to make them look like heroes again, and Lucan Dlere was able to leverage Roley's failures and Valeron's "running off again" appearance into a massive wave of support, allowing him to seize the city. When the Knights of Truth have spent a whole generation helping everyone but the actual people they live with, it's not hard to convince the common citizens they're a bunch of glory-seeking hypocrites.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: Do you know if Champions of Norrath and Champions Return to Arms are cannon?

answers.author: Lore
answers.text: So, you've stumbled on the biggest and most touchy question in all of Norrath lore, ever. What is canonical and what is not. It really really depends on who you ask. Most people will say that they are not canonical but that they utilize canon. My personal take and approach to lore is that ANYTHING officially licensed can be considered canonical, even if the story being told isn't the same we see elsewhere. History is full of conflicting accounts and translations get changed/misinterpreted over time. As soon as I get to dig into EQL's unique lore, I'll start incorporating it into the overall stories/timelines I've been working on for ages. There's also a lot of "what is canon" that changes. Ex: historically, a lot of people would say that EQoA was not canonical to EQ/EQ2 but time has made a lie of that. A lot of EQoA locations and/or storylines have been continued or canonized by the games. Even tricker because you have things like Nektropos Castle. Nek was in the EQ beta files but never made it as a live EQ zone. So the first time we encounter Nek Castle is in EQ2 and then in lore stories in EQ1 via DoN, I think it was. BUT, you can kinda say it's technically canonical from EQ1 because it was always there. Tower of Rot was also a beta EQ zone that wasn't in game. It was present in EQoA and hinted at in EQ2. Eventually got put into EQoA during the Ethernere tainting happened. I piece them all together for a cohesive story as I can. Actual OG lore wasn't as cohesive as we'd like to believe. There was far less of an overarching plan originally. A lot of lore and story was dev specific and based on who worked on what zone and some of those stories are completely lost if they weren't properly or adequately documented. It's why you find dead end quests and the like. You also had live quests that changed the world and content that pre-dated those live quests was lost. If you can't recover it or find evidence of it, is it canonical? Our lore devs, past and present, are greater tale weavers - pulling those threads together

answers.author: Lore
answers.text: Of course, the staff that contained Cazic's divine essence is stolen. (Cazic, himself, is in the Ethernere). The divinity was stolen by the gods of Alaris, a continent that has been hidden from Norrathian's view since the Age of Scale. Their return rips away the veil that keeps Alaris hidden from Norrathian view. The gods of Alaris, after transporting their people to Norrath and putting up the Veil, existed but were essentially powerless. We find out that Alaris was a group of people from another world on the prime material plane. Alaris was invaded by Discord and Order was losing so the Alaran gods transported the remaining Alarans to Norrath. This all happened in the Age of Scale, before many of our current pantheon ever came to Norrath. The Alaran gods felt they had to act because they'd sensed the incursions of Discord on Taelosia and the influence of Discord during Seeds of Destruction and so they put in place a plot to manipulate Cazic's kids into attacking him, releasing his power (or getting it trapped in a staff as the case may be) in order to steal it from him so that they could resume a true godly state and protect Norrath from Discord. Several Norrathian gods team up to free Cazic's essence (including Rallos, Solusek, Prexus and Morrell). Enter Rain of Fear. Our destruction of the Alaran god amalgamation causes an explosion that rocks Norrath and releases Cazic's divinity, which falls down onto Norrath in the form of crystalline shards. The largest and the heart of his power appears to have dropped on Odus. > The largest, and the heart of his power, dropped onto this previously unknown plateau, just missing the hole, and creating a crater. Many smaller shards also landed. So presumably the Grand Plateau. We do a lot of things and basically stop another Alaran god from stealing Cazic Thule's power to become Norrath's new god of fear. Luclin, who walks the path of balance, then takes the heart in the Plane of Shadow to safeguard it until the power of worship can revive Cazic Thule.

answers.text: Unbeknownst to players in Norrath during the Age of War (Turmoil where EQ starts ends at around Depths of Darkhollow if I recall correctly), another god in a future and different form of Norrath has been killed. In EQ2, Rallos Zek has been killed due to his plot to sync the plane of War with Norrath to fight The Sleeper. Adventurers work together with Tallon, Vallon and Sullon Zek to use the combined swords of destiny to kill Rallos Zek, sending his spirit/soul into the Ethernere while Cazic's spirit is also there. The influence of the two dead gods in the Ethernere causes a corruption in the Ethernere, with souls being siphoned from adventurers. The spirit world is on the verge of collapse. Souls are escaping the Ethernere and the Harrowing Horde (think Wild Hunt) seek to reclaim them. Simultaneously in the EverQuest 2 timeline, The Sleeper is trying to get Lady Lendiniara, the powerful dragon prophet. She is a member of the first brood and is the oldest dragon living on Norrath. The Sleeper uses the Tear of Veeshan to go after her. Her chronomancers perform a ritual to send her through time to escape Kerafyrm. While she's escaping, she hears a voice calling to her and she follows it.

answers.author: jifypop
answers.text: Just above me, a perfectly circular object descended from the sky, spinning on its axis. Blue light streamed down from its bottom in a shaft, searching the course of its descent. It was capped in an iridescent dome and made sounds unlike any creature I'd ever seen. At first, that's what my child's mind thought it might be: a mockery of a flying beast, terrible in its extreme mutation. It came to rest some twenty feet above the ground, directly above my head, and when people appeared suddenly in that shaft of light below it, I thought maybe they were jumping out of its mouth. It was only later when I went inside that I realized it was some kind of craft, like a coach, but one that could fly. When the blue shaft vanished and the people came to full view, I found them to be neither human, nor elf, nor goblin, nor ogre, nor anything else I could name. One stood at the front of the group, nearest to me, and his eyes were deep green, pupil-less orbs, his skin a pale green, and hairless. He stepped forward, and the crowd inhaled sharply. He was only a hairsbreadth from me now and he leaned down so that he could peer in my eyes. I even remember that he smelled different, like nothing I could name, but it wasn't unpleasant -- no, I remember thinking it was a very fresh smell, like clean blankets. When he spoke, I couldn't understand what he said, and I merely stared up at him with a mixture of curiosity and terror. He seemed to wiggle something near his ear, and then when he spoke, I heard clearly: "Is there disease here? Has the Xulous force reached this world?"

answers.author: jifypop
answers.text: It was as if speaking broke the spell. Some people panicked, running from the sight, while others drew swords and nocked their arrows. Still others yelled that we should talk because he had come to save us, for as it happened disease had swept through a neighboring region and claimed lives with the unbiased carnage of a great fire. By then though, my mother found me and swept me up into her arms, holding me to her chest tightly and backing away. I watched the man as she went, and he watched me, the bottomless depth of his eyes unmoved. I lifted a hand and waved to him, and he smiled and waved back. Turning to the crowd, he said, "Please don't be afraid! I've brought medicine! I'm here to help you, not hurt you!" As my mother drew me further and further away, his words were drowned in the roar of the crowd, but I still remember his face, so many years later. A face I would later come to know as that of a god. And help he did. It took time but eventually they routed this force he was pursuing, the "Xulous", and healed those who were still alive. Those who were there say he performed great miracles, that he was able to bring people back from the very edge of death so that they walked and talked as healthy individuals once again. My mother would later boast about how we had been there, forgetting of course, that it was she who drew us away, and about how I was the first person he ever spoke to. In doing so, she maintained, he had bestowed on me his blessing of perfect health. This seemed plausible enough until a few years later I fell into a deep sickness, not the plague that had ravished us but an equally dangerous malady. It seemed I was done, but the great healer was to visit me for the second and final time.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: Fair enough - any recommendations in the YouTube realm?

answers.author: Lore
answers.text: Classic EQ isn't "a" story. It's many stories and you get to pick which one(s) you pursue. The lore comes in all forms - item lore, environmental, through books and notes that drop, spells/abilities, autonamous npc actions and then actual dialogs with npcs. Random npcs that don't give quests will still talk to you and you can ask npcs questions that aren't just the highlighted text. Use the 5 basic questions to see if you can get more information. You used to have to actually cast identify on loot in order to get the item lore. Also, learn languages. Some npcs don't respond to common. Classic isn't like live or wow. It's like d&d. What you get is based on what you do. Some people love to dig into the world while others just want the dungeon crawl. There's more than you think but what you get is based on what you do. I've done some videos on some topics, going deep into them but I've had trouble approaching classic because of how it's presented. I'm planning but still in research stages for classic prehistory. Going through the Ages now after deep diving into creation, planar structures and deities.

answers.text: , , , Norrath wasn't actually created on purpose. Brell Serilis accidentally made it, the other gods showed up, and everyone just pretended it was part of the plan. The biggest secret was that Cazic-Thule and Innoruuk were together for centuries. Fear and Hate ended up falling for each other, which absolutely drove the rest of the pantheon crazy. Tunare wouldn't acknowledge it, Mithaniel Marr acted offended every time they showed up together, and Bristlebane spent most of eternity making the rumors even worse. At the same time, Brell kept bragging that dwarves were the perfect race while Tunare insisted elves were superior. They eventually tried proving it by mixing the two together. Instead of getting the best qualities of both races... they somehow created trolls. Nobody could explain why combining a dwarf and an elf resulted in a giant green swamp monster, so everyone just agreed to stop asking questions. The trolls wandered off into Innothule, started hitting things with clubs, and history moved on. Rallos Zek saw the trolls and thought they needed to be bigger, so he made ogres by removing most of the intelligence and replacing it with muscles. Veeshan also didn't create dragons. She just found them living on the nicest mountains and claimed they were hers because nobody wanted to argue with dragons. Most EQ historians will tell you none of this is canon, but that's exactly what someone trying to hide a centuries-long romance between Cazic-Thule and Innoruuk would say.

answers.author: Gannor
answers.text: Honestly, I've come to suspect the symbols on the Chelsith Stone appear in Neriak, the Spectre Tower in Oasis of Marr, and in the Plane of Hate in reverse of their creation on the stone, rather than being copied onto it. Especially since there's nothing I've seen to indicate the Dark Elves pre-date the Shissar.* * Yes, I know, there's a solid argument the Y'dal do. That's another kettle of fish. The Shissar were gifted with Knowledge by Zebuxoruk, it's not hard to imagine others had access to Zebuxor and could have recieved insights. Not going into that here. In Neriak, the most conspicuous placement of the symbols is with the Witches, which makes me wonder if they hadn't been scried or spied through oraclular means. Innoruuk is good at his little spy networks. I think he was trying to find a way to lay claim to the prophecy, rather than the Shissar having somehow gotten it from him.

answers.author: Gannor
answers.text: Since Al'Kabor tells us that the symbols around the Chelsith Stone are a timeline of events depicted in symbol, and a series of instruction in glyph, I think it's safe to assume the central figure is Veeshan, since the point of the thing is the Age's Eng Prophecy - culminating in stopping Kerafyrm's intention to usurp Veeshan, as the climax to a completely Dragon-focused war and Dragon-focused series of events.

answers.author: Gannor
answers.text: And, true to the suggestion, Mayong was involved in unearthing the stone itself, so that it could then be reclaimed and put its series of events in motion, thus fulfilling his piece in the puzzle.

answers.author: Gannor
answers.text: I'd also note that the Chelsith Stone is only one of the Monoliths. The actual Shissar Calendar covers more than that, as the Book of Sunder itself reports.

answers.author: Saberine
answers.text: So Originally in Everquest, you had Tunare create the elves, they were the Elddar, they lived in whats now The deserts of Ro, which before the curse of solusek ro, (who was jealous of tunare's creations) was a vast fertile land, and the original birthplace of the race, the elves progressed by blending magic with nature, until at some point their creations were more magic then natural, this lead to a group who preferred natures purity, rather then arcane infusion to split off, they sailed off and landed on the land that became known as Faydwer, (This part im a bit murky on) they eventually settled there in the Faydark, and befriended the dwarves, who had been placed there by Brell Serrilis, Eventually the druids of the Elddar couldnt hold back the curse of Solusek ro, possibly due to Innoruuk kidnapping their king and queen, and slowly torturing them into what is now the dark elves, The Elddar that fled to faydwer this second round, ended up known as the High Elves, they landed on Faydwer right around where the dwarven docks are now, and ended up journeying (Severely diminished in population at this point) to Greater Faydark where they met what had now become the wood elves, the high elves didn't wish to live in nature anymore and created the city of felwithe, during this time the dwarven stronghold that became known as crushbone was taken over by orcs, which has kept the elves preoccupied since.

answers.text: To summarize the New Seb lore: -Some hundreds of years ago, during the reign of Rile Sathir, an expedition was sent to Antonica. -This expedition landed in North Ro. They were digging in to entrench themselves when they broke into some surface ruins of Takish’Hiz (the elven dungeon from LDoN) -The Iksar built into the ruins to make their base, and discovered a library in the process. -books in the library detailed the Elves’ attempts to use sand magics to preserve the city and themselves as its guardians -The Iksar attempted to repurpose these magics to build new golems (the big clay guys you see in Sebilis and other places) -They did create golems, but the golems responded as if defending Takish-Hiz and slaughtered all the Iksar or suffocated them in sand.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: Been wondering for a good while what the Sarnaks worship, since most races tend to worship their creator god, and Sarnaks are an artificial creation by a mortal, yet have access to Holy and Unholy magic which you need to directly be gifted from a god (At least to my understanding) which is why Necros and Rangers can't be agnostic. Any clues?

answers.author: Lore
answers.text: Druidic magic is less holy and more natural or nature based. In Norrath, nature isn't just a thing that exists. It's embodied via gods like Tunare and Karana. If you don't serve at least some aspect of their goals, they could (and arguably would) revoke access to that aspect of themselves. Essentially severing that connection. Druids are priests of the natural world. Shamans of the spiritual (a la animism) and clerics the divine. Holy/unholy is reserved really for the divine category. Necromancers are inverse priests of the discordant gods. They fit under the divine category. You can learn of necromancy but you can't practice it without serving a discordant aspected diety who grants "safe" access to those discordant energies so that we, orderly creations of the prime plane, can use them. (Void/ discord corrupting is what happens when you try to access discordant energy without it being filtered through members of the celestial order as the energy is naturally entropic.) Rangers are warrior druids and sks are warrior necromancers so they follow those rules

answers.author: aderyn
answers.text: As far as I’m aware they worship their own emperor, Bathezid Di’Zok. They had some political connection with the dragons, but it was not a warm relationship, so I don’t think they were paying any tribute in that direction.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: whats the deal with runneye, there are two goblin clans and they are both fighting the evil eyes? How many revamps were there? Whats the lore?

answers.author: Batmanuel
answers.text: I was looking at last night to see what's changed since quests were written in perl. I found Lord Pickclaw has dialogue explaining their story. He responds to three keywords, but I can't find out exactly where you learn to ask him about the ritual.

answers.author: Batmanuel
answers.text: "hail" Hail? You should be on your knees, charname..! I suffer you in my realm for the moment, but if you and yours keep on with your attempts to destroy us, this will change. Do not think for a second that my subjects will hesitate to do what I command. I have proven myself in battle time and time again, and will do what is needed in the future. Xorbb learned this the hard way, and I am ready to teach this lesson to anyone else who challenges me. "xorbb" Surely you know of Xorbb? The leader of the evil eyes, his home is in Beholder Gorge, which he calls his own. That will soon change. We drove him out of our ancestral home here, and we will drive him out of 'his' gorge as well. We shall not forget what he subjected us to, his foul minions controlling the very thoughts of our people, enslaving us to his bidding. But he is weak now, weaker than ever before, and we will take advantage of this weakness. Mark my words, the gorge will be cleansed, and all evil eyes will learn the true meaning of revenge. "ritual" We are the Pickclaw. Once we were of Runnyeye, but when Xorbb corrupted our king and took over the citadel, we fled, risking death in the caverns of the Serpent's Spine rather than submit to Xorbb's twisted rule. We grew strong in the tunnels, learning much about warfare and survival. We honed our skills against the masters of High Keep, and we learned much about the ways of magic from those we captured. But we never forgot where we had come from, and we vowed to one day return. When I saw that Xorbb had grown careless and complacent here, while our clan had grown strong, I took back our home. The name Runnyeye it shall keep, as a reminder of who we WERE, but all who I suffer to live here must prove themselves, as Pickclaws, for this is who we ARE!

answers.author: aderyn
answers.text: See the above, but the basic revamp timeline IIRC is: Classic: Runnyeye is run by the Runnyeye clan under the thrall of King Xorbb Prevamp: run as an event for a short time, Pickclaw clan invades Runnyeye, both goblin clans are present and fighting on various levels Revamp: Clan Pickclaw takes over, a few scattered Runnyeye remain on the top floor. I’m not sure if the Sporali were around through all versions of the zone or if they came with the Pickclaw. They’re not listed on old mob lists that I can find.

answers.author: aderyn
answers.text: Ogres are interesting. They shouldn’t necessarily *be* hostile to most people. Yes the Rallosians wanted to take over the world, but they’re not xenophobic like Dark Elves, or just depraved killers like Trolls. They’re not even slavers like Iksar. They wanted to conquer and *incorporate* other people into their empire. They’re EQ’s Roman model. I think post-curse, the only reason they are the way they are is because the Dark Elves took advantage of their diminished intellect and manipulated them.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: I mean, worshipping War is pretty hostile. Not the same maliciously personal way as worshipping Hate or Fear, but they were always aggressive to others werent they?

answers.text: Sure, but aggressive in the expansionist, empire-building sense. They’re not averse to the idea of working with other people, as long as those people are working for them.

answers.author: aderyn
answers.text: The whole foundation of the Rallosian empire was cooperation with other races, with all the various Rallos races serving in their defined roles in the army. Ogres as the generals and tacticians, Orcs as infantry, Ankexfen as arcane artillery, Giants as siege weapons

answers.author: aderyn
answers.text: But in the lands they had already conquered they built *cities* and had arts and culture. And presumably those cities were populated. So it wasn’t like the entire Rallosian civilization was constantly at war.

answers.author: Vhaen
answers.text: Iksars and slavery

answers.author: aderyn
answers.text: When Morell Thule cast Mithaniel Marr’s gift of life into the swamps, it wasn’t just Innothule. The whole point of the scheme was to create something to help weaken Cazic’s power on Norrath. So he put Frogloks in Antonica to battle the Trolls, and he put Frogloks in the Swamp of No Hope in Kunark to battle the Iksar. That second one didn’t work out so well. The Iksar Empire was strong at that point, and they just captured and enslaved the Frogloks. Atrebe Sathir even used them as guinea pigs in his magical experiments. After the Empire fell, a number of Frogloks were able to escape back to the swamp and create a new home, which is a sort of mini-Kelethin looking place called Krup. That’s where the free ones were as of EQLive, hiding out in the swamp being constantly raided for slaves by Cabilis.

answers.text: ## General Tips - You can stealth when using a ritual portal or quick buff - Start casting your ritual or quick buff then hide/sneak. answers.author: Lore
answers.text: Some old school lore here, pasted in parts hopefully. No idea if Az plans to use it or not. > Proper service in the Eyes of Innoruuk is expressed by three commandments. In Neriak, past the Third Gate, in the Black Library, there is a small chamber. In that most holy chamber stands a pedestal, and on that pedestal rests the Great Pact. Here is written in the Ancient Tongue the Commandments of Innoruuk by His own Hand. These are the foundations of the Church, and must be followed above all else. I set forth here, in plain and modern language, the Commandments:

answers.author: Lore
answers.text: > THE FIRST COMMANDMENT: PURPOSE > > All TeirDal were created only for the fulfillment of the Will of Innoruuk. We exist only to do so. We do not follow the Will. We ARE the Will. We cannot be separated from the Father, and free-will is not a burden We carry. We are not troubled by questions of right and wrong as are mortals. We simply do the Will of Our Father, and in this We are superior. > > Each TeirDal is given a purpose in the Will even before their birth. We Children must follow Our purpose, for only in it will the Will be realized. Above all others, some purposes are great, and are called the High Purposes. They are enumerated in the Litany of Purpose and are as follows, in descending order: > > The Queen and King: Eternal Mother and Father to Us all. They are pure, and beyond reproach. > > Clerics: They are the mouth of Innoruuk and speak His Words. They insure that Children do not stray from the Father, and that the body does not falter in the Will. They are one with the Father and above all others in understanding of the Will. They are His embodiment in this world. > > Necromancers: Their purpose is to command the dead in the service of the Will. Death is no excuse to be released from the Will. The dead must serve the Father as in life. There can be no rest until the End. They also bind the dead of the Hated Others to the Service of Innoruuk, and are to be revered. > > Shadowknights: They are the Soldiers of Innoruuk. They are the holy guardians of the Priesthood, and the swordarm of the highest servants of the Father. They are unwavering in their purpose and are blessed in the Eyes of Innoruuk. > > Warriors: They are the shield of the Queen and King. They are strong among the Children, and full of Hate. Their purpose it to cut down the\par enemies of the Will and before them none shall stand. > > All purposes serve the Will of Innoruuk, but these shall be set above all others as most holy.

answers.author: Lore
answers.text: > THE SECOND COMMANDMENT: UNITY > > TeirDal shall not raise word, hand, or sword against TeirDal. All are Sisters and Brothers in the Will of the Father. Those that turn away from the Will, however, shall be considered Spurned, and shall be treated as are the Hated Others. The Will shall always remain open to them, however, and if the Spurned turns back to the Will of the Father, they shall be allowed admittance to all but the highest mysteries of the Church, as befits the purity of their blood.

answers.author: Lore
answers.text: > THE THIRD COMMANDMENT: PURITY > > The teachings of the Church shall not be kept from any who are called to the Will of the Father. Therefore, all who turn from the lying gods and turn to the True Father may be taught of the Will, regardless what race they call Mother. However, those not of purest Teir`Dal blood shall not be taught the inner mysteries, nor allowed entry into the Third Gate or the Church of the Firstborn. They shall also not partake of the Greater Ceremonies, nor be bound by the Commandments of Obedience to the Father. In short, they may be taught Our Father's use for them, but they are not to be admitted into the Circle of His Children. > > Those that stand against the Father shall be damned. They are the Hated Others. All shall be reviled and destroyed. Hatred shall be spread among them and they shall perish from inside as well as from out. No mercy shall be shown them, and none shall be suffered to live. > > Thus are the Words of Our Father. Thus are His Commandments to Us.

answers.text: # Getting Started The [EQL Wiki](< exists because our community makes it better every day. If you see something that’s unclear, missing, or could use a little love, don’t wait for someone else to fix it — go ahead and improve it. Every contribution, big or small, helps keep this living resource growing and up‑to‑date for everyone. When you’re adding a new page, don’t worry about making it perfect. Making things look nice matters too, but the most important step is simply creating the page and saving it for the first time. Anyone can edit almost any page. It’s definitely a work in progress, and not always the easiest read — but there are gold nuggets tucked inside. answers.author: bob
answers.text: A note: We have an AI content policy: Aside from ethical concerns, the reason for this policy is because AI generated content doesn't come with any guarantee, or even a vague promise, of accuracy. I just spent several hours confirming data from an AI-generated page, and every single section had inaccuracies stated as truth. Every. Single. Section. The goal of the wiki is to provide accurate data, as much as we can. If someone wants to submit a page, they need to understand the subject well enough to provide accurate data. If they don't understand the content well enough to check it for accuracy after an AI writes it, all it does is create more work for everyone else. While it is a community project, please do not submit articles without confirming the data. It's very rude to spend five minutes telling an AI to generate an article, but then expecting other people to do hours of work to clean up your mess.

answers.author: Caliente
answers.text: Yes, unfortunately we are still in a state with AI where it can fail us at both: - AI created content, even if re-written by a human, can still be flat out incorrect, wrong and made incoherent, incongruent, hallucinated, etc. - Human created content re-phrased by AI and pasted... even I use this on paragraphs where I fumble to explain things eloquently without putting a lot of mental energy into it; and the AI can complete fail at getting the fact(s) or message(s) I meant to get across, and if you don't proof read it *again* and make any needed corrections, it will read like AI garbage. AI still can't tell the difference between EQ and EQL half the time it seems.

answers.author: Caliente
answers.text: 1080p still dominates the viewer screen resolutions today, but we try to make it look good for all sizes if possible! As for standards on what to use, we try to match what is in game unless it doesn't make sense to modern gamers -- for instance, the majority of gamers are going to call jewelcrafting, jewelcrafting, and not jewelry making, which is the term sometimes used in game. The biggest problem with EQL is that it isn't consistent in terminology -- it tries to deviate sometimes and not always consistently. So, go with what you see in game if it makes sense, otherwise use what players will understand best. South Ro for the Southern Desert of Ro isn't hard to figure out, but just make a judgement call on how much room you got. SRo is what most ~~players~~ veterans call it today.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: what's the point of putting your name in the page title if not to claim it as your own?

answers.author: Caliente
answers.text: You're no wrong, you're describing the social psychology of wikis, not the software behavior. I'm not wrong, I'm describing the technical reality of MediaWiki. I need to revise the help page to reconcile both. My point is: - Pages in the main namespace are fully editable by anyone. - Pages in the user namespace are also editable by anyone unless manually protected. - MediaWiki does not enforce ownership based on page titles or names. You're point, I believe, is: When a page title contains a person’s name, it implies authorship, and many editors interpret that as soft ownership, even if the page is not protected. I have merely been trying to seek clarity and how to describe all of this to wiki editors who have never discussed the topic and want to know this.

answers.author: bob
answers.text: That's why I put my name in the title But putting it in my userspace makes it even "more" my own, because it looks to be protected from edits

answers.author: MAERGOTH

answers.author: MAERGOTH

answers.author: Amerzel
answers.text: I’d like to get the class spell descriptions updated and consistent. I have one proposal for that here

supportingEvidence.author: Amerzel
supportingEvidence.text: # Issues Right now the class pages mix different description and effect columnn styles. Some show level scaling, some don't. Some of the effect columns actually scale past level 50. Before I clean these up, I' like to get some feedback and consensus on the format. # Columns Is it useful to have both "Max Effect" and "Description" columns and have them separated? There's a lot of overlap between the two and ultimately they typically convey the same general information. Not all spells have an effect. ## Max Effect Some spells scale beyond the curernt level 50 cap, should we be showing max spell values higher than the player can actually reach? Some spells scale to 60, 70, 90, etc. Some bard songs scale indefinitely. Example: [Togor's Insects]( shows Decrease Attack Speed by 49% (L39) to 70% (L60), at L50 the Slow is 60%. * Do we want to show what the effect is at the spells max level even if the player can't get that high yet? * Slow: 70% * Do we want to show what the effect is at the current player level cap? * Slow: 60% * Do we want to show the scaling between initial and max spell level? * Slow: 49% (L39) to 70% (L60) * Do we want to show the scaling between initial and player level cap? * Slow: 49% (L39) to 60% (L50) ## Descriptions Widly inconsistent verbage across classes: A lot of classes share spells and the same spell reads differently depending on which class page you're on: Minor Healing example:

answers.text: > dannuic — 5/18/2026 10:30 PM > okay, here's what I have. First sheet is the log2 formula, and the second is values I copied from the wiki. I hope it's okay I copied the formatting koss, but it was the easiest way. You can see things that are expected NO in the first column are what's not observed in game, the first sheet has no errors while the wiki ones have some really small ones that only manifest in weight (so far) and only when it's a big weight > > Google Docs > Review of Bulk Data Collection, with Item Check > > The basic formula is just some variation of this: original_value * (1 + (int)scaling*log2(total_progression)) where scaling is -0.09 for weight (it's well known for EQ that weight is sent from the server at 10x the value and then divided by 10 in the client for display) and scaling is +0.1 for everything else. total_progression is just the complete progression points, so a tier 4 item is 16 progression, while a tier 4 and 3/16 items is 19 progression. You can get this from tier and progression as just 2^tier + tier_progression (so 2^4 + 3 = 16 + 3 = 19 in that last example)

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: The quest would be repeatable, right? How many +0 would you need to get to +3 to pull the exalt?

answers.author: MrCatSmith
answers.text: 8 ish?

answers.author: ThatCAT
answers.text: At that point you probably just want to drop motes into it. You need an uncommon bracer and with new drops from Crush the ring mail might be tricky to get.

answers.author: Mkb617
answers.text: It’s exponential. You need two of the previous to make the next so 2,4,8,16,32 etc. So if starting at 0 you need two of those to make a 1 and since you need 2 ones to make a 2 that would be 4 zeroes to make a two. Another way to math it is to think of it as powers of 2 so 2 to the 3rd power is 8. So if you want to get to +10 it’s going to be 1024. That is where upping difficulties helps. So instead of starting with and using a 0 you are starting with a +4. It’s not a huge difference but it helps

With raid encounters, I found that it was important to upgrade charm. For the longest duration possible, Tash and Over Channel were used. I found Over Channel + Tashania could still be hit and miss; sometimes it would cause charm to last almost the full duration other times it wouldn't. If charm broke on a boss encounter, I would inversion stance usually to get it back up. During these encounters is the only time I would actively heal my charm. I rarely used Promised Renewal on myself, but it did have a place when relying on a buffed-up charm pet to tank. I found that the best charm targets were (in no order) clerics, paladins, monks, rangers, and shamans when paired with a warrior base. Enchanter, Mage, Necro, Shadow Knight, and Beast Lords were never a long-term priority charm. Then most of my pet gear was warrior-specific just for the biggest range of application.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: And that helps, how? The motes improve cast time and resists, and "maybe" the level of mobs that can be charmed? But how does it factor into charm breaks?

answers.author: Jokon
answers.text: I don't have the *current* code but what's been sussed out over the years is that charm breaks are triggered for two reasons; first, there's a basic chance to break charms that is flat. Second, every tick (six seconds) the charm makes another magic resist check just like when you first cast. If that core system has changed then my info is out of date. When you level a charm spell, both checks are easier. The flat break chance is reduced to zero at +10. The second is easier because the innate MR you're checking against is lower and lower per spell level.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: Have not had the chance to try out the ENC pet, thus, have a question for those who did (well, some questions, actually): - Is there a way to control the pet like a MAG pet (via AA, maybe?) or is it purely reactive like in classic EQ? - a druid pet buff would apply to the ENC pet, correct?

answers.author: Shines
answers.text: The pet did have the default controls as per the mag pet out of the box. Experience with charm seems to be all over the place- some people adore it, some people hate it. A d4 three-class mob will, by my understanding, become a d0 three-class mob. It maintains it's class abilities but loses the difficulty modifier of the zone. There's also no dire charm, so maybe you hit your pet with mako and tashani, and while your odds are better, there's no promise that it won't break twice in three minutes. For me those things combined to make charming just not worth it but other people swear by it.

answers.author: bob
answers.text: But to answer the original questions: Yes, you can control the pet with regular commands. Also, if you buy the Alternate Ability called Companion's Discipline: Single-target buffs can always be applied to the pet. Once you get the Pet Affinity AA, group spells and songs will apply to the pet, and you'll also need it for the Quick Buff AA to work on the pet.

answers.author: cerotoneN
answers.text: I'm running War/Shm/Nec and was curious about Fangol +10 vs Garduk +10 and Dagas +10. I asked our buddy chat gpt to run some numbers, and here's what I got. Could be AI slop but I had it taking its time coming up with an answer and was referencing eqltools.com, eqlwiki.com, and eqlegendstools.com. I had it assume a level 50 Warrior with all relevant melee AA's: > Weapon +10 damage/delay, Ratio > Fangol, 58/35, 1.657 > Garduk, 46/40, 1.150 > Dagas, 22/21, 1.048 > > The dual wield chance break-even point with Garduk and Dagas against Fangol is: 48.4% > So Dagas needs to swing successfully only 48.4% of the time for the dual-wield setup to pass Fangol in raw weapon ratio. > The available level-50 Warrior estimate places the pre-AA dual-wield chance around 54.74%, although the wiki explicitly labels the underlying formula conjectural. EQL’s exact combat constants remain unpublished. > > There are two plausible readings of the Ambidexterity AA: > > Multiplicative: 54.74%×1.32, 72.26% > Additive: 54.74%+32%, 86.74% > > Either interpretation comfortably exceeds the 48.4% break-even point. > > Results: > DW chance and Lead over Fangol > 54.74%, no AA, +4.0% > 72.26%, multiplicative AA, +15.1% > 86.74%, additive AA, +24.2% > > Thus, before damage bonuses and activated attacks, Garduk/Dagas is plausibly 15–24% ahead. Of course, Garduk is an outlier, the ratio on that weapon is insane.

answers.author: cerotoneN
answers.text: It goes on to factor damage bonuses: > As a sensitivity check, suppose Garduk has an 8-point bonus and Fangol has a larger 12–15-point bonus. Dual wield then breaks even at approximately 55–59% offhand success. > > That is still well below either reasonable Ambidexterity estimate (additive or multiplicative): > > At 72.26%, dual wield remains roughly 7–10% ahead. > At 86.74%, dual wield remains roughly 15–18% ahead.

answers.author: cerotoneN
answers.text: > Fangol still wins on attacks that are specifically primary-slot based: > > A Fangol primary hit uses 58 weapon damage versus Garduk’s 46—about 26% more per ability hit. > Rampage performs a primary-slot combat round. > Burst of Power’s flurries occur after a primary-slot triple attack. > Riposte-related attacks generally favor the stronger primary weapon. > > Therefore: > > Ordinary autoattack and Cleave: strongly favor dual wield. > Rampage, primary flurries and ripostes: favor Fangol. > Overall sustained melee: still favors dual wield.

answers.author: cerotoneN

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: Curious to what everyone thinks is the best to combo Shm with in-wise of DoT stacking? At level 50. What is the Dot Stack with Shm/Dru? At level 50. answers.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
answers.text: In Open Beta i did SHM-NEC-PAL. You get the Shaman and Nec DoT AAs plus the generics and they all stack. DoT wise if you're really serious about it you can cast eight of them on a big boss. Best dmg DoTs were Odium (VIII), Envenomed Bolt (VIII) but the others are good. NEC has a flame dot which is great against things which are resistant to one of your other lines. I ran Slugs to VIII and it was fantastic. With the AAs affecting beneficial spell duration + focus effect it lasted for 54s and healed ~250 a tick. I would normally cast it with Empower and pick up another +15% since I had two non-hybrid casters in my loadout. You can pre-cast it before fights too. Puma adds huge DPS to your pet. At VIII with the AAs and focus I think my Puma lasted for 3:30 or so and proc'd for 200ish. If you stand around in Empower, your procs will benefit from Empower, so when you're just meleeing and waiting for DoTs to expire I would milk some extra damage from the proc. My overall DPS against D4 stuff was ~280-320. I had decent stuff but no sky gear, and my planar/dragon gear was ~+3-5. Pet added about 60-70 with SHM buffs, haste, and Puma. My own DPS was 80% DoTs, 6% white damage and the rest was misc. Cannibalize is wonderful, heal back up with Slugs.

answers.author: Callius
answers.text: LOY is 15 min reset, every time you smite it reduces it by 1 minute, berzerker stance means your melee skills reset twice as fast, thus you get double the smite hits, likely look LOY every 3 minutes or so Berzerker stance will eat endurance though, need shaman or ranger end regen buff Personally i only enable smite auto skill when LOY is down , due toi the also 3% mana drain per smite

answers.author: Deleted User
answers.text: Smite is not a proc. It's a combat skill based on a timer that will autofire (when enabled) each time the timer is up. It is not linked to dual wielding. It can double and even triple attack if you have that skill. It will drain 3% of your total mana when it lands but will convert that mana into damage. So the larger your mana pool is, the more damage it does.

answers.author: Xel
answers.text: I think a few of you may be confused about the AC softcap. Hitting the softcap and not caring about more AC after that is the wrong approach. Every point of AC on your sheet past the softcap is just as good as the points of AC before your softcap. It just takes more AC per stat sheet point than before the softcap. If you’re at 600 AC on your stat sheet and somebody else is at ~400 and not caring because they reached the softcap already, that person with 600 is going to take a lot less damage. The softcap only affects how hard it is to get more additional full points of AC

answers.author: ManiiNames (5k2k Club)
answers.text: One takeaway I have from your list is you’re spending a slot on regen (Chloro?) and haste. Both of those should have ~15m duration with the AAs, focus item, and maybe upgrade to +4 or so. I would move those to a separate spellset, mine is called Short Term Buffs. That would free up two spell gems for other things. If you were really serious about it you could write a macro along the lines of: - /pause X, /memspellset myCoolBuffs - /pause X, Cast Haste - Cast Chloro - /memspellset myCombatLoadout I did not have a macro like that which I used regularly, because I grouped just enough that I had other targets I wanted to cast the spells on. So I would just use /memspellset MyCoolShortTermBuffs and then manually cast the spells. Was also handy for buffing the pet if it needed haste or whatever. I tend to run six spellsets minimum, for each loadout. Name them appropriately so you can tell which loadout they belong to. Combat, Perma Buffs, Buffs, Short Term, Pet, Raid

answers.author: Lye(x) - (Bryan)
answers.text: I cannot confirm but /pet leave should work

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: because im a little slow today, this macro is helpful when your charm breaks mid battle, yeah? that's the idea?

answers.author: Lye(x) - (Bryan)
answers.text: That is correct. You start by setting a target you want to charm as xtarget slot 1. /xtarget set 1 currenttarget. Then you use the macro any time to recharm. You can use it mid battle and you will quickly save your current target (slot 2), then choose your previously marked charm target (slot 1), the drop into overchannel, start casting charm in gem slot X (put a number here), and the retarget what you originally had targeted (which you had JUST saved to slot 2).

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: would it make sense to end the macro with /doability [insert previous or most used stance like inversion] ?

answers.author: Lye(x) - (Bryan)
answers.text: You only get 5 lines in a macro. So you COULD macro out the rest but 2 things: 1. 6 second CD to swap invocations back to whatever you were in. 2. It would put you in THAT invocation, not whatever you WERE in. So the macro would then dictate what you go back to, which may or may not be what you want... These 5 lines are the required to one button recharm with no interruption to targeting. It would likely be even better if you added more and more lines. I would LIKE to add: Save current target Cast Mez Swap to charm target Cast Whirl (assuming I am in a fast cast stance at this point) Tash Auto Attack to break mez on charm target while he is stunned Go to Overchannel Charm Go back to original

answers.author: Lye(x) - (Bryan)
answers.text: In one button, without having to manually calculate time on when to fire off the second macro and all that. But even so, the macro I shared should help if you want to increase your fanciness., or chain more stuff together. I could see a benefit for writing one that recharms out of combat to reset the clock as it were Dismiss Pet <- It'll hit ya and make you target it if no other enemies are Whirl it pause Tash but no 6th line available to pause then charm, but you could just use the OTHER macro to charm.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: WIth the EQL system of permanent gear for Pets, what have you found are some key concepts to use for equipping them?

answers.author: Cyanide Bunnyslayer
answers.text: Since all necro pets below 50 are WAR/SK, you will want to focus on gear in this way: - AC and HP if your pet is going to tank. HP Regen is helpful too - STR for increasing chance of maximum damage - DEX for increased weapon and buff proc chance - AGI for increases dodge chance - Mana and Mana Regen (mana Regen doesn't exist in classic EQ, so this is for future expansion) - Haste to increase auto attack attack speed The pet won't benefit from STA, WIS, INT, or CHA A LOT of research is going into pet weapons, but generally you want to dual wield weapons with procs, and you want to seek out weapons with at least 25 base damage AND a delay of 30 or lower (ratio of 5/6 or better) which are rare in classic eq.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: I would love to see Ranged stance do something else & have the Double & triple attacks work with ranged based off an AA (like 9 points?). Maybe Ranged damage gets a bonus based on the distance from the target?

answers.author: serrasin
answers.text: Archery with endless quiver and the ability to keep out of melee range is essentially free infinite damage, the various bonuses just increase the rate of application. i know, duh, just wanting to underscore that archery has an inherent and distinctive advantage if you are able to take advantage. Face tanking your target is obviously a solution granted by ranged stance, as is having a pet or party member tank for you. If you have sufficient run speed then you can circle kite the target, or root & shoot, or reduce its speed to zero (such as a snared mob fleeing due to low health), or fearing it. Those are some very surface level tactics, but there are still others. For example, using constant stuns and whirls. As things stand now most bosses are resistant if not immune to most CC effects, so pet tanking is the most efficient solution since ranged stance eats up endurance like tequila shots in a singles mixer. If I were to make a suggestion to the devs for mechanical changes prior to seeing parses to gauge the real world difference between archery and other dps strategies, then it would be to fold the mechanics of the ranged stance into Mastery of the Scout - spreading them out across the ranks. This is less about pure power and more about removing a obstacle from allowing archery to synergize with other classes and abilities.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: oh really? the quiver was empty and it still worked?

answers.author: Diogenes
answers.text: Yes. The game has never cared if you had an arrow in the quiver. That was always some stupid myth that people came up with and others ran away with it. The other stupid myth was that it had to be in a specific inventory slot, it does not nor has it ever. The game simply checks for a WR quiver in inventory (in any base slot, such that it can act as a container) and then grabs the WR% to calculate with. It doesn't matter if you have multiple, it takes the highest WR% the same way you can wear 2 haste items and it will only use the best to calculate with. The only real question here is if GJ changed or broke anything, and it appears that nothing is different so it works as expected.

answers.text: From natch potes: - Stunned players now receive a short-term immunity from additional stuns that lasts beyond the duration of the current stun. This will prevent chain stunning. However players beware, NPCs also learned the basics of this skill.

answers.text: We dont know how far beyond the duration of the current stun. It could be something as simple as a 3 to 5 second "stun immunity" on a mob after a stun wears off. Players get the same treatment. The exact duration for both is currently unknown but I would expect them to be the same. Whats good for the goose and all that. I cant imagine it being less than 3 seconds or that much more than 5-7 seconds on the high end. Chain stunning is simply gone, for both players and NPCs. Overall a good change, but I hope its not gonna end up eating Enchanter aoe stuns. But chaining Whirl til your Hurl will no longer be a valid strat, and is likely part of the reason players got this nerf too.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: The AA change just made more questions for me. I totally understand the correction/clarification that it works with DW. What I do not understand, is the rest of it. How exactly does it use the Secondary or Any Slot item? Between competing items, how does it determine which is preferred? Is the item's AC and/or damage relevant to the damage calculation? Does Slam work similarly?

supportingEvidence.author: Tarr
supportingEvidence.text: Right, i see they just changed it. Okay I just did a bunch of testing. I took off my weapon and the items in my any slots, so attacking unarmed, my bashes hit for 1 damage consistently. I equipped a 12 AC shield with in the secondary slot with no weapons and the bashes were hitting for good numbers. Highest I saw was a 128 crit. Regularly hitting for 35-70. It worked the same in the any slot, I didn't notice a damage difference. I tried the same thing with a low level 1 hander and no other weapons/shields equipped. 10 base dmg, 6 bonus dmg. The damage was a little more volatile, I saw more hits in the 12-17 range, but it would often still hit in the 30-60 range, but normally closer to 40. Highest crit was 110. Same thing with the 2 hander, +6 BABS, 34 base, 12 bonus dmg. The damage seemed a bit better than the one hander, but about the same as the crappy shield. Highest crit was 142. Commonly hit for 40-70. But given the damage difference, I would have expected BABS bashes to hit way harder, so I think either damage is normalized, or it doesn't make a difference what weapon/shield is equipped and the damage difference I noticed was a placebo effect. I should try with some other items with a much greater range of damage/AC, although BABS vs that 1 hander is a huge margin so I dunno what's going on there. Each one of these tests had no other items equipped in the weapon or any slots. I did test with ONLY a piece of high AC armor in an any slot and the damage was still 1 as if unarmed, so it is for sure only taking into account weapon or shield, as the tooltip says. I also saw a disproportionate amount of 40 damage bashes with all weapon options. I didn't parse any of this, but I feel like around 15-20% of all non crit bashes were exactly 40 damage regardless of weapon/shield. Not sure what's going on there.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: It looks like they changed the tool tip for Improved Bash? It only says it will use the best AC from equipped 'weapons or shields'. I think it said any item yesterday?

answers.author: Tarr
answers.text: Right, i see they just changed it. Okay I just did a bunch of testing. I took off my weapon and the items in my any slots, so attacking unarmed, my bashes hit for 1 damage consistently. I equipped a 12 AC shield with in the secondary slot with no weapons and the bashes were hitting for good numbers. Highest I saw was a 128 crit. Regularly hitting for 35-70. It worked the same in the any slot, I didn't notice a damage difference. I tried the same thing with a low level 1 hander and no other weapons/shields equipped. 10 base dmg, 6 bonus dmg. The damage was a little more volatile, I saw more hits in the 12-17 range, but it would often still hit in the 30-60 range, but normally closer to 40. Highest crit was 110. Same thing with the 2 hander, +6 BABS, 34 base, 12 bonus dmg. The damage seemed a bit better than the one hander, but about the same as the crappy shield. Highest crit was 142. Commonly hit for 40-70. But given the damage difference, I would have expected BABS bashes to hit way harder, so I think either damage is normalized, or it doesn't make a difference what weapon/shield is equipped and the damage difference I noticed was a placebo effect. I should try with some other items with a much greater range of damage/AC, although BABS vs that 1 hander is a huge margin so I dunno what's going on there. Each one of these tests had no other items equipped in the weapon or any slots. I did test with ONLY a piece of high AC armor in an any slot and the damage was still 1 as if unarmed, so it is for sure only taking into account weapon or shield, as the tooltip says. I also saw a disproportionate amount of 40 damage bashes with all weapon options. I didn't parse any of this, but I feel like around 15-20% of all non crit bashes were exactly 40 damage regardless of weapon/shield. Not sure what's going on there.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: I am running enc/ber/pal and my only issue is smite draining mana. If the solution is just not smiting I have been thinking about replacing the pally with a cleric because if I can't smite why even have the pally?

answers.author: Shinra Kuonji (Twice Punished)
answers.text: Consider reframing the way you view smite. It's not an always on thing like other class features. It is a high impact way to convert resources into damage very quickly for when fast damage takes priority over other things. And it comes on a class that does not normally have the ability to do anything like that. Paladin's usual methodology is that slow and steady wins the race. So, being completely outside the classes normal wheelhouse, it comes at the cost of being inefficient. And that's okay. This provides you an avenue to make a choice as player as to how you want to spend your resources, and particularly, how quickly you want to burn through them. This is where metering the usage comes in. If you've got excess Mana to spend, click the button. If you're barely scraping by trying to survive, don't push the button. Not everything needs to be automated and active all the time.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: heyas thanks for the reply-- I cant pally atm as my primary is SK--- what are your thoughts on SK zerk sham?

answers.author: Shinra Kuonji (Twice Punished)

answers.author: Shinra Kuonji (Twice Punished)
answers.text: Additionally, as long as you have a priest class in your mix, I think Paladin and Shadow Knight are largely interchangeable. Their overall power level is very balanced, so I think the difference is mostly just role-playing aesthetics. Likewise, Togor's Insects is one of the most impactful spells in the game, so Shaman and cleric are ultimately interchangeable for most things as well, although their playstyles end up very different.

answers.author: Shinra Kuonji (Twice Punished)
answers.text: One of the key factors that people tend to overlook when discussing the power level of promised renewal specifically is that it requires you to play predictively. You need to cast the spell far in advance, before damage has actually happened, and you need to be able to predict how far in advance to cast it so as to not waste healing, or not die. It's efficiency especially over the long term is largely dependent on the player's ability to do that. This also means the spell is much more powerful insights where enemy damage is very predictable and consistent, and much less powerful in fights with unpredictable spikes such as the eov. Likewise, if the player can't predict the damage consistently and time the spell properly, it loses a huge chunk of its value. More conventional heels like what the shaman has do not have this consideration. One of the big counterpoints though is that Shaman does not have much in the way of big burst heels to get back on track if things start to get out of control. With their heel over times and such they are good at maintaining your health at a consistent level, but if you drop into the danger zone, they can struggle to get back out of it.

answers.author: ❄Ẕ𝕐𝕃𝕀𝔼❄
answers.text: Varies based on which stance you're using for delays, but effectively like this... Line 1: /pause 25, /cast 1 Line 2: /pause 30, /cast 2 Line 3: /melody 3,4,5,6 Where the first 25 pause is equal to a 2.5sec cast + gem refresh time, and the secpnd 30 sec pause is equal to a 3.0 sec cast and gem refresh time. IMO calculate the cast & gem refresh then add like 3 to the delay to ensure server delay doesnt clip it for the hotkey to work every time. But remember if you are in a stance that lowers either casting OR gem refresh, then being out of that stance will jack up the hotkey cuz the timers will be all off. But thats the gist of making a multi-cast hotkey. If you want this to also kill yoir current melody to refresh the 2 first dots add a /stop to the first 2 lines instead and mo v e thise down to lines 3 to 5.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: I was told in General to make it a priority to upgrade the Instrument of Nife self buff - does it actually increase the damage of the proc? What about any other self buffs. Can some pros help me here please?

answers.author: Shinra Kuonji (Twice Punished)
answers.text: Proc buffs like Nife deal one ranks worth of damage per two ranks of actual upgrade. So you always want to upgrade it in even numbers. Very much worth it. At rank 8 it does a little bit north of 300 damage. As for other buffs, they do not gain potency from upgrades. They only gain duration, reduced cooldown, and reduced Mana cost. So upgrading other buffs is purely a quality of life question. The notably, he'll overtime effects like celestial cleansing do gain potency with each rank, as well as duration increase and Mana cost and decrease. So buffs and heal over time effects are operating on a different set of rules.

answers.author: Shinra Kuonji (Twice Punished)
answers.text: Also, just to clarify: buffs not gaining potency from upgrades is entirely by design.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: ty-- was wondering about melody chants-- do i ahve to turn off melody, then charm, then reactivate melody to apply chants to next target? and if so does that cancel charm? or---- if i do charm, then i cant melody my chants?

answers.author: Boisterous
answers.text: I wrote up a little bit about bard macros here Melody isn't a thing that has to be turned off - you interrupt it when you cast, but you do have to turn it back on. Bard songs don't get cancelled, they run for a duration and then end. Charm, like mez, is cast on a mob, lasts for a duration, then ends. So you can charm a mob and then immediately start casting other songs or spells until the charm wears off and you need to cast it again. So yes you charm, then melody a few songs, then charm again when it wears off. Depending on which charm you're doing and what you've upgraded it to, this could be 18 seconds or upwards of 90.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: Pets are locked at 30 delay? So if you use a weapon with faster delay, does it still go to 30 delay?

answers.author: ⚡RizikRanger⚡
answers.text: Yup

answers.author: Essay
answers.text: Its not as simple as that being locked to 30 delay based on the testing others have done (this is for summoned pets only). Here was the best summary I found and my testing shows the same outcome: > Cudgel of fools reduced my pets swings to 5-6 seconds. Earthshaker with a higher delay is 2-3 seconds Yes, this is because Cudgel is a better ratio weapon than the pet's base ratio, so it uses both the damage and the delay of the cudgel to take advantage of it's higher ratio. Earhtshaker even though it has very high damage has a lower ratio than the pet's ratio, so the pet just uses the weapons damage but with the pet's default swing speed (30) so an Earthshaker when used by a level 10 BST pet becomes a 74/30 weapon which is way better than the Cudgel. Cudgel maxed out is 90/52 which is a 1.73 ratio Earthshaker on warder is 74/30 which is a 2.46 ratio Hope this makes sense."

supportingEvidence.author: straydogsteve
supportingEvidence.text: There was a post on the subreddit I read about this. Ranger gets much better returns than 1 AC per 10 past soft cap. Credit to the OP “smurfalidocious”: “There's several threads, and you can even look at the softcaps in the game files themselves in EQL\Resources\ACMitigation.txt. The AC Cap is a 'soft' cap, at which point the Soft Cap Multiplier comes into play. Looking at the first entry, it reads: Warrior at level 1 has an AC Softcap of 312 worn/buff AC, after which every point of AC past 312 you get 0.35 AC per point beyond. At level 50 (1^50^410^0.35) a Level 50 Warrior will cap at 410 worn/buff AC and get 0.35 points for every point of worn/buff AC beyond that. Conversely, the line (2^1^274^0.3^) is Cleric at level 1 has a softcap of 274 AC and each point past that provides 0.3 points. Shields aren't affected by the soft cap multiplier and always provide their full worn AC benefit. These are just the base values, too, and don't take Combat Stability into account, which pushes the armor softcap up by a flat percentage. And yes, AC buffs from spells count towards the softcap, and provide the same diminished returns when you exceed it. For the softcap returns, rather than make everyone look through this file to find per-class, here they are: Warrior: 0.35 Paladin/Shadow Knight: 0.33 Ranger: 0.315 Cleric/Monk/Bard: 0.3 Beastlords/Berserkers/Rogues/Shamans: 0.28 Druids: 0.265 Enc/Wiz/Mag/Nec: 0.25 That's also not quite the whole story since Warriors have an innate 5% damage reduction - essentially the RNG that does damage calculation can never roll a 'max' result against Warriors, only the second-best result, which pushes them ahead of Knights for tanking innately even beyond the .02 softcap they have over knights.”

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: So, from this, I'm guessing that the Weight (Worn) is not a binary for Monks. It's not 'overweight' or 'not overweight'. If this is true, is there a minimum value for Weight (Worn) where AC is no longer a concern, or does the penalty start at anything greater than 0 and slowly go up from there?

answers.author: SeppTB
answers.text: 31 is where the bonus stops, though that moves as you level I believe. Its when the worn weight value goes red that you are no longer getting any bonus. But yes, its as you state, the bonus scales by your worn weight, the lower the better, so increasing weight can offset AC gains. I carried about 6 different items while leveling as a monk that on their own did not increase my AC because weight increase offset it, until I got a 7th heavy item that then equipping all 7 at once and entirely dropping the bonus made each of them an AC gain. You can also get the Packrat AA to decrease worn weight to get back in range, but then end up back in the same land of evaluating weight vs AC

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: Unrelated, but I saw people discussing SK/WIZ/BRD in here and I would like to play it. What would my rotation and gear look like?

answers.author: anarth
answers.text: Standard lustrous russet, inny/sky gear, and then bloodmoon + sky shield for mh/oh. have a shield in your any slot so you can get at least 3 of the instrument focus effects equipped. You’ll have symphonic aura with 5 songs taking up 5 spell slots. The rest is up to you but you will be rotating frost/fire rain spell and then casting conflag or rend x2 or x3 and then casting the rain spell again while in Arcane Mastery 2. You’ll do this over and over until the boss is dead. In addition, before a fight you’ll want to be in overchannel and charm the highest level / quality multiclass mob you can. With charm at lvl 8 you should have about a 2 min charm and it virtually never gets resisted or breaks early if you use overchannel first. You’ll want to refresh charm when it breaks during a fight but once you get geared enough you’ll kill everything before it even breaks the first time.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: how do you get the pet to keep threat?

answers.author: Cyanide Bunnyslayer
answers.text: It surprisingly holds aggro well. Don't over nuke and rip aggro, and if you do, back off until it gains it back. Against raid bosses, the mob will ignore the pet if you are in melee range so keep that in mind, however the pet will still occupy a spot on the hate list. The simplest way to maximize pet aggro is to maximize pet damage output. Give it two weapons with good procs, give high STR, DEX and ATK from buffs and gear, and spam Frenzied Burnout on cooldown. Spell Casting Subtlety also helps to reduce YOUR aggro. And if you have Feign Death from your other classes in your trio, use it

answers.author: Cyanide Bunnyslayer
answers.text: If you are coming expecting vanilla EQ pet aggro, you will be pleasantly surprised at how much better the pet can hold aggro here

answers.author: ThatCAT
answers.text: I've been doing sky with the level 46 earth pet rank 10 (whoops): As above you want to stack threat procs (stuns ideally), either on weapons or through BST buffs- Hobble of Spirits (AA) is also great because Gonar will also spam snares. FD is the only way you're going to be able consistently damage the boss, but this will not always work: occasionally it seems like threat is reset on both pet + master. Unless you want to chain summon them you need to be able to slow the boss and cripple helps that much more. Having an actual healer to support them goes a long way (cleric or shaman, sorry druids). I'd be prepared to walk into melee range if you can't land a slow or your pet is about to die.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: it should be at 0.71 ratio and he stayed the same as a +6, what did i do wrong?

answers.author: nlaak
answers.text: Most weapons only upgrade the ratio on the odd pluses (+5, +7) because of how they math the merging and the magnitude of the bonuses from +0 to +10.

answers.author: Kyou

answers.author: nlaak
answers.text: Some items will get mid level upgrades. I first noticed it on the Flaming Fists, which have a fairly high save vs fire. I've yet to see a weapon ratio change mid level - I've only seen it on the level increase, and virtually always on the odd levels. The reality is that there are usually (always?) less than 10 actual upgrades for weapons, leaving some levels not getting a boost. That's just the way the math works out. Anyone thinking otherwise doesn't understand the math/code that makes it all work.
