answers.author: Chuxbe
answers.text: Some DDD theory and parsing thought below. Goal is to get the most damage out reliably, in a single mana pool, to a real pull of mobs. TL;DR: Pick based on what gear you have to maximize mana pool. Ignoring that, best damage should be out of Wiz/Ench. Read below to see why. (*maybe* someone can go insane end game and squeeze a wisdom build through itemization to hit another breakpoint to tip the scales to a wisdom build) Theory Class Options (mana pool source): Sha/Dru (wis) - You can get more wisdom items, and a higher mana pool, with two wisdom classes. You get druid crit AAs. You get canni V for (almost) 2 more DDDs. With canni 14 or 15 casts for most decent equipment holders. (never arcane) Wiz/Ench (int) - wiz crit AAs, Ench is the best utility class for DDD (mez + provides mana pool buffs). Up to 16 casts with arcane mastery, 13 with empowering Wiz/Dru (int) - You double the spell crit AAs. 12 or 13 casts with strong int gear and empowering (never arcane) Breakpoints: - ~8775 mp for 13x casts with empowering invo @675 mp per cast (believe that's on the high end of range. saw 645 too). Wis builds should be shooting for around this. - ~8640 mp for 16x casts with ~~arcane mastery~~(use recovery if you want lower mana cost. AM not working to that effect) (with int classes at least) @540 mp avg per cast (surprisingly mana cost per cast varies. From what I'm seeing 540 is about middle of the road/enough for the passive mana regen to ensure you get enough even if your average on a given pull is higher). With 8788 mp total I always ended close to another cast. Could be achieved with some more int gear work. Note: - A lot of damage is wasted on pets/mobs that have current hp < DDD damage. On all killing blows you waste some damage due to the excess. Parsed Findings On 5 dummies. no resists. Enough samples to convince me well enough: sha/dru (wis) - ~297k empowering wiz/dru (int) - ~277k empowering wiz/ench (int) - ~320k (not empowering)

answers.author: Chuxbe
answers.text: Conclusions sha/dru (wis) Someone could push this up with a serious focus on wis gear. Major negative is that you don't have aoe mez, and minor negative is that you don't have the minor mana pool bump ench gives you. Positive is you get damage out faster due to empowering and that you get Canni for another 1k mp. Wiz/Ench (int) Both parsed the best and I expect it to have an additional MAJOR positive in real pulls because your average DDD cast is less damage, therefore less damage wasted on casts that kill mobs (doing damage over the mobs remaining HP). Medium negative is that damage gets out slower (lower mp per cast, lower dmg per cast). Pretty sure this is the GOAT setup in arcane mastery invocation. If talking about only empowering I expect wisdom to beat this with good gear. Wiz/Dru (int) I thought it would be the strongest due to double crit. I wasn't seeing that in the crit rate or the resulting damage. Still insanely strong, and you get damage out fast with invo. Interested if anyone else has other tips to squeeze every bit out of this silly DDD thing until they nerf it in to oblivion. Let me know what I missed in the analysis! (small disclaimer - all of this is assuming you have all relevant AAs maxed out, DDD lvl 10, etc. Proper races for mana pools (wis = HIE, int = ERU). Gear in pretty good shape (5+ everywhere relevant)

answers.author: BC
answers.text: It's very good. Much better than charisma

answers.author: reborn as  fishermin
answers.text: AC to softcap is very high value. imagine you take 100 damage per sec but have 1,000 hp. now imagine you take 50 dmg per sec but only have 500 hp. (traded +500 HP gear for AC gear) your regen heals you for 50/tick. which character is stronger? (this is just an example. other stuff matters--but AC is very nice)

answers.author: tev
answers.text: yeah its a combo of the concept explained above plus the fact that other stats dont give very impressive returns per point. Resists are very strong too but have weird returns (they don't really do anything until you get enough of them, and then they do alot, and then after a certain point you're already immune to spells and they stop doing stuff again)

answers.author: tev
answers.text: And then once you factor in indirect gains - less damage taken / time spent debuffed or stunned = more time spent doing damage instead of healing - it lends itself to AC and resists generally being the most important stats on gear

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: Is there any reason to NOT merge motes at the golem dude in town?

answers.author: khantrol
answers.text: Yes if your leveling spells it's better to not merge them. And if you can level other items then put the result into the main one its better to not merge. 3 + 3 = 6 xp. 3 and 3 merged into a 4 is 4 xp etc.

answers.author: Baelas
answers.text: Absolutely. Points are lost along the way depending on which motes you merge and for what you use them. The system is weirdly complicated and lossy but suffice to say that half the points are lost each time you merge infitesimals. And anything above "mote of potential" yields vastly reduced upgrade points for items, but give their full effect for spells. On the other hand there's never a need to merge for the purpose of upgrade spells since all motes are allowed in all spells. In short, you can merge motes up in order to upgrade items up to +4 without much loss except the 50% loss from infitesimals. If you have the option it is better to get multiple items and upgrade them to +4 and merge, rather than to merge potentials.

answers.author: khantrol
answers.text: Really the only reason to merge mote is if you trying to level up a rare item and need the higher tier motes to do it.

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: Anyone with ideas on what BIS would look like for sk wiz enc?

answers.author: malkavon
answers.text: I haven't sat down and crunched the numbers on exact pieces (other than just what seems to be clearly the best options I've found), but: Earring of Bashing/Something Else (ENC sky earring is decent, Ivandyr's Hoop is decent, honestly upgraded Adamantite Earring or Drop of Crystallized Flame aren't bad on their own - classic Jewelry is pretty sparse) Bloodstar Pendant or SK sky neck; or Talisman of Kejaar Kerrath (I wear the former with the latter in an ANY slot; if you feel you don't need the regen, the former is the best I've found stats-wise and packs all-resists) Darkbrood Mask or SK Sky mask (I prefer the former for the resists and mana, though it does lack MR) Umbral Platemail Helm (I haven't really found a better hat, but there are a decent number of sidegrade options here) Engineer's Ring/Ring of Pureblood or SK Sky ring (ring of pureblood has slightly worse stats all things considered, but offers HP/Mana; SK Sky ring has better AC, slightly better relevant stats, and SV Magic which is a premium stat) Verishe Bracer of Dominance/Lustrous Russest Bracer (or just two Lustrous Russet bracers if you find yourself swimming in them; reasonable stats and good resists) Midnight Clad Armbands (decent stats and OK resists; not the best resists but still nice-to-have) Slime Blood of Cazic Thule (decent AC/HP/Mana, all stats and all resists that scale very well with upgrades) Umbral Platemail Breastplate (best AC in slot, solid stats) Pauldrons of Power or SK Sky shoulders or Imbued Granite Spaulders (solid stats on both Pauldrons and SK sky shoulders; I consider these sidegrades; IGS has amazing AC and resists) SK Sky belt (best haste item you can get, which affects Reave CD; another option Cryosilk Belt (or something compatible with the Extended Range III Focus Effect) Cloak of Scales (good stats, AC, excellent HP/Mana, can take ID3 focus) Lustrous Russet Greaves (good AC and solid stats) Midnight Clad Footwraps (decent stats and great resists)

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: is bash and slam really the same exact skill? if so, why was I able to ogre slam w/o improved bash while dual wielding and having a shield in the ANY and not bash? Did I really just waste 6 AAs on improved bash for no reason if I'm going to stay ogre?

answers.author: magusbones
answers.text: They’re on the same cooldown. Don’t know what slam scales off of or if it interrupts spells like bash. Go gnome

answers.author: Thomas
answers.text: Slam does 1 damage, any class can use, skill is effectively always 1. Warrior, paladin, and sk can get bash up to 240 (warrior) or 200 (knight) and it does good damage. The aa lets you do it while dual wielding, etc.

answers.author: Dumesh
answers.text: Slam racial ability has it’s hit rate and damage scale based on your bash skill. If you stay Ogre/Troll/Barb, the AA is less valuable than for other races, but it will let you use bash instead of slam which can scale to a higher damage number by using the AC of a shield you put in your Any slot. qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: what were the dot revamps?

answers.author: Undr
answers.text: Long ago, in an alternate universe, in a land much like our EQL norrath here… All dots had rather low base dmg, but they all stacked. You had druids running around with a dozen different versions of stinging swarm dots on their bar. Shamans and necros running every rank of heat blood/poison dots, diseases, curses etc…

answers.author: Seped
answers.text: They made a big effort to move dots into 'lines' of spells, so instead of being able to stack your 4 highest fire dots, you could only use the best one. To go hand in hand with this they also boosted the damage of dots to compensate for losing the lower level dot stacking. Then they applied this system to all the cool dot classes like druids and shamans. Proud of the work they had done they took a break saying "We'll get to the rest soon." Meanwhile necros cried softly in the corner for the next decade (and counting).

answers.author: Undr
answers.text: Then daybreak, decided in their infinite wisdom, to revamp the dot lines, increasing the spells power, but not allowing stacking. Buff/debuff slots were limited and all the dot classes would eat up all the slots on raids, it also made for a pretty sad “gameplay loop”. enter the dot revamp, more oomph, no stacking of the same line

answers.author: Socrathustra
answers.text: So I think I've compiled my list of major mechanical issues with melee: * No way to contribute to melee accuracy outside of stance and monk; compare to overchannel + resistance debuffs + caster level AAs + mote leveling * Melee endurance gets eaten faster the better your gear is; compare to mana costs decreasing substantially with motes * The above are doubly compounded for pets which have even fewer tools * Stances other than berserk or offensive give up half your damage; compare to invocations being flavors of casting which all have offensive use * The strength of charm pets was previously offset by the risk/reward factor given enchanters were so squishy, but they're not anymore * Combat abilities do not scale whatsoever the way spells do My recommendations to fix it: * Allow dexterity to contribute to accuracy as its tooltip says * Create a precision stance similar to overchannel with a 50% accuracy bonus but half the damage bonus (with later changes, this is 75% of current offensive stance) * Bring melee damage WAY up across the board, but lower the bonuses for the offensive stances (probably 50% and 50%) - tie it to stances still though so mobs don't start wrecking us * Permanent pets need their own stances to compete * Flat endurance expenditure normalized to swing speed that does not depend on damage output * Allow us to level combat skills with motes

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: If I am past AC cap is it still the most important stat? For example - would AC 20 shoulders be better than AC 10 shoulders with +25 stats I use (str/int - I play shd/wiz/enc)?

answers.author: Kharnor
answers.text: AC is still the most important stat, but you do still need to weigh how much other stats an item brings. For example, if im also trying to stack mana and health, I might take one item that has a bit less AC and has much higher of health/mana.

answers.author: Kharnor
answers.text: Always use a BP, robe(if mostly caster), or shield in your any slots to maximize AC

answers.author: Kharnor
answers.text: The AC cap is the starting point btw. I think some people hit it, and think they are done stacking AC, when the reality is that you need to stack waaay past that if you want to be comfortable being in something like offensive/ranged/berserker stance in D4 against bosses and such

answers.author: Kharnor
answers.text: As a personal rule, I try to at least get around 550AC. That is the point where I feel comfortable always being in a dps stance in D4.

answers.author: Kharnor
answers.text: Resists are also extremely important. This is another area I see people make gearing mistakes. They will stack AC and health thinking they are tanky, even though their magic resists are like 100 or sub 100. At 250 MR you resist most things, and at 300, you basically resist everything

qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: Could you share that macro by chance? I haven't figured out a way to get the pet to engage and disengage for variable periods of time using the same button press. Or is it 2 different macros?

answers.author: Janus (Tashan - Neriak Server)
answers.text: You need pet ghold on for it to work, otherwise he'll burn mana with other spells or cast heal anyway once you hit under 50%. Once Pet Ghold is on and you're fighting, it's simply /pause 40,/Pet attack then on the second line /pet back off. THis will trigger a heal. Next to it, have pet attack and pet back off so it's easily clickable. Use those two when you want to ride his healing when at something like 25% health to 50% Reason for pause first is because oddly, the way macros work, the pause is counted at the end of that line when in front of the command

answers.author: Bugrup
answers.text: Personally, I'd go Bloodmoon / Shield. Bloodmoon's damage is as good or better than most 2H, and only a little lower than the four of five (that I know of) with better ratio : Khyldorn the Blood Drinker is a lot higher DPS though Plus, you get the extra AC and stats from the shield. qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: Ostorm in the Sol Ro temple will not accept Rubys nor affirm that he can reset your specialization through his quest. I had no idea that your subsequent character loadouts could have different specializations and my second loadout ended up specializing in Abjuration (RNG/ROG/WIZ) . Has the quest moved or is there some other way to reset your specialization?

answers.author: Black Triad™
answers.text: I see this quest was removed for some reason so I wasted some AAs ang got Master of all 1. Trying to raise a second specialization seems to be bugged as the skill raise message keeps coming up and won't go beyond (50) . [25 RNG ROG WIZ]

answers.author: ShadowFae
answers.text: There are multiple bugs going on. 1) The game will reset your specialization to Abjuration when you level a second caster loadout up to 30. You can't stop it. You will be an Abjuration specialist and you will like it. 2) If you buy Mastery of All 1, you can choose a second specialization, but at some point the game will reset you in alphabetic order - so you'll get Abjuration and Alteration. You can't really stop this, sorry. 3) When you buy Mastery of All, you will get skillups showing you're stuck at 50. This, at least, isn't a huge problem; it's a display issue. Log out and back in and you'll see it upgraded the skill. At this point, you need to buy all 4 ranks of Mastery of All to avoid the resetting specialization bug, which is *very annoying*.

answers.author: ShadowFae
answers.text: The quest itself isn't bugged, it just doesn't exist here. You're supposed to use Mastery of All to get the specializations you want. But the resetting thing that makes you have bad specializations messes it all up. *In addition*, if the quest *did* work it would just waste your ruby because the game will then undo it and give you Abjuration back xD

answers.author: Black Triad™
answers.text: This is messy as hell and needs to be addressed. This is not the only fubared issue either.

answers.author: Black Triad™
answers.text: Oh, I "do not like it" either.

answers.author: Syllus
answers.text: I thought so too Maergoth, but I went digging and found some info from the original devs: > - Two-Handed Bonus - If you use a two-handed weapon, you get an additional amount of bonus damage. This bonus is the one you see listed on two-handed weapons. This bonus varies depending on your class, level, and the delay of the weapon being used. Slower weapons get larger damage bonuses, than fast weapons do. All two-handed weapons of a given delay receive the same damage bonus, for example a level 60 warrior with a 40 delay two-handed sword gets a damage bonus of 23, as listed on the weapon. That's a quote from which itself is quoting a dev Q&A (couldn't dig up the specific Q&A). Searching patch notes, I only got a hit on one from 9/19/2000 which says: > ... two-handed weapons have had their damage-bonus modified. > The damage-bonus for low-delay two-handed weapons (27 or below) created > a problem similar to the weapons above and has been reduced. qa:https://discord.com/channels/14357864.question: I have my air pet using my Indicolite armor. When I swap to a different non-mage loadout with my warrior, it loads the armor. When I swap back to mage, instead of the equipment going back into the pet inventory, it's dumped into my Equipment or inventory storage. Any ideas how to fix this? Or is this a known issue?

answers.author: Anachrony
answers.text: Yes, I have problems with this too. It doesn't seem to save pet equipment as part of a loadout, but it really should. Pets can use equipment that matches the class of the character, and have different classes of their own depending on what type of pet they are. So that alone is plenty of reason that the equipment is totally different between layouts. But also you may want to emphasize different stats based on whether they're a tank pet, DPS pet, or charmed. It's annoying to have to manually fix the pet equipment every time you change loadouts. It becomes doubly chaotic to manage if the pet from one loadout uses the same equipment as the character in another loadout.

answers.author: Anachrony
answers.text: Similarly, there are problems managing exaltation slots between loadouts. Certain exaltations might impose extra class requirements or compete with other exaltations that are better for some classes than others. So it's often necessary to swap out exaltations based on loadout. Or sometimes you want the same exaltation in the same slot, but the loadout has a different item in that slot. It seems like any time you move around exaltations it doesn't save and restore them properly, so you have to manually adjust it every time you swap loadouts. It's very annoying to manage since it takes a lot of time to figure out the best exaltations for each slot and go through every slot and try to remember what belongs there.

answers.author: Boisterous
answers.text: As a new 50 his gear will not be anywhere near yours, esp since he doesn't have any Innoruk gear yet or CT. He might be undergeared as you say though and could use a couple plane of hate or fear runs for a pretty solid boost.

answers.author: Boisterous
answers.text: As far as songs go I would drop psalm of warmth and run elemental rhythms. Make sure you have a drum exalt equipped. This will help with his big DD spells. Put largos melodic in your SA - the slow is 35 percent which is almost double Selos chain. You should put some motes in it to make sure it doesn't get resisted all the time. Mine is at 9, but you can probably get it to about 4 and be ok. You should probably toss a HoT on yourself and then only use drain soul as your main source of healing. If you mote it up it will lifetap for around 700hp. Even at level 5 it will be a significant improvement and nearly unresistable. So basically debuff, using over channel put your dots up, switch to inversion and lifetap the hell out of him. As the poster above says, some runs of the planes for gear will make a huge difference. As you get more AC, you take less damage, which means evasive stance uses less endurance, which means you don't run out as quickly, which means you don't have to spam heals or sit in channeler stance.

answers.author: Boisterous
answers.text: As far as SA songs, you get marginal gains by running all three regens vs cantata. (I think it's plus 2 mana/endurance to run all three) Id recommend you run cantata for Regen, largos melodic bunding, elemental rhythms, guardian rythms, Jonathan's war song (lvl 45 I think). It should cap your haste, slow Innoruk, buff your resistances, and still give you decent regen. If it turns out you're running out of endurance or mana specifically, swapping that specific regen song might be worth it. The alternate path is full turtle, where you just keep yourself alive and put up all your aoe dots and your single target chants, switching from channeler to evasive and just trying to dot him up, keep the per charmed, and outlast him. I can give more specifics if that's the route you go, but I think you'll get it with a charmed pet and some motes into drain soul, tbh
